claims.text: Damaged high-value components can have physical and microstructural characteristics that create a risk of hot cracking.
A hybrid remanufacturing intervention can combine additive manufacturing, surface strengthening, and subtractive manufacturing.
Additive manufacturing can be combined with numerical-control machining to improve part accuracy.
Micro-forging, laser shock processing, and shot peening are suitable surface-strengthening elements of the proposed hybrid intervention.
The intervention is intended for service in aggressive environments under high stress and high temperature.
Surface strengthening can refine the microstructure produced during additive manufacturing.
High-frequency ultrasonic impact can break up and refine coarse dendrites generated during laser-directed energy deposition.
Surface strengthening can reduce residual tensile stress and introduce compressive stress.
High-frequency ultrasonic impact applied with laser-directed energy deposition can transform tensile stress into compressive stress.
Rapid melting and solidification during laser additive manufacturing can generate residual tensile stress.
Microstructural refinement and compressive residual stress improve resistance to wear.
Microstructural refinement and compressive residual stress improve corrosion resistance.
Hybrid remanufacturing will improve surface characteristics relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated surface.
Hybrid remanufacturing will reduce hot-cracking risk relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated surface.
Hybrid remanufacturing will enhance wear resistance relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated surface.
Hybrid remanufacturing will enhance corrosion resistance relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated surface.
The proposed intervention avoids whole-part replacement while minimizing costly deposition equipment, pollution, and long processing times.
The effectiveness of hybrid remanufacturing may depend on the material, strengthening technique, and manufacturing process.
A comparative experiment can evaluate hybrid remanufacturing against both fusion-welded and untreated controls using surface roughness, microhardness, corrosion resistance, and wear resistance.
Failure to obtain significant improvements in surface characteristics, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance against both controls would falsify the hypothesis.
